newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian share index regains from recent lows.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian share index regains from recent lows.

text.p: The Egyptian stock market regained some of its lustre on Sunday as recent problems with a new dealing and clearing system appeared to improve, brokers said.
Shares had fallen to a two-month low by close on Thursday after trade was plagued by delays in the systems.

"Now the clearing house has cleared 42,000 unsettled trades, and we are optimistic about how the market was behaving," one broker said. "Some of the prices picked up and volumes picked up for a lot of stocks.
Another broker said there were still problems with the systems but he had also noticed an improvement.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 0.1 points to 232.78, up from Thursday's 232.68, its lowest level since August 19.
Turnover slipped slightly to 21.67 million pounds ($6.37 million) from Thursday's 21.86 million pounds.
Brokers said the banking and housing sectors were busy, but the popular flour mills were the most active although prices were generally lower.
East Delta Flour Mills fell 0.1 to 35.90 pounds and Central and West Flour Mills shed 0.26 to 52.24.
Blue-chip Commercial International Bank regained some strength, closing at 443.5 from Thursday when it fell 20.00 pounds to 440. "CIB started picking up today," a broker said.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 352.42 from 352.55 points, while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 163.08 from 162.94 on Thursday.
Seventeen rose, the same number fell and 27 were steady.
